items.title: OpenAI shares physical engineering experiments
items.summary: OpenAI describes using ChatGPT and Codex for mechanical design, electrical engineering and simulation. Its thread calls these early steps and says engineers review the outputs; these are company-reported examples, not independent validation.

items.title: Brockman describes Pando, a Git backend
items.summary: Brockman says Pando handles large monorepos while preserving familiar Git workflows. He is considering making it available to others; the post is an invitation for interest, not a public product launch.

items.title: Altman says human control should constrain AI progress
items.summary: Altman says people should not cede control of the future to superintelligence and that this requirement should limit AI progress. This is his stated position, not a published enforcement mechanism or a demonstrated safeguard.

items.title: Pachocki brings Madry back to work on AI’s pace
items.summary: In his October 19 post, Pachocki says he asked Aleksander Madry to return to OpenAI to work on the pace and implications of AI progress. The post describes a research and strategy focus; it does not announce a development pause.

items.title: Brockman shares new scientific claims
items.summary: Brockman announced results across mathematics, computer science and physics. OpenAI describes the manuscripts as raw research material and sets out different release and expert-review arrangements. We have not verified the proofs.
items.contextLabel: Read the release and review approach

items.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI presents Terra as a faster, lower-cost option for visual reasoning and computer work. Its performance comparisons are company evaluations; test complete workflows before relying on the model.

items.title: OpenAI explains its offline training environment
items.summary: OpenAI says frontier training uses cached web content without live internet access. Its infrastructure retains necessary connections; the announcement describes a containment policy, rather than independent verification of its effectiveness.

items.title: OpenAI responds to the outside monitoring review
items.summary: OpenAI says the summer pilot with METR and Redwood helped strengthen its safeguards. Read the evaluators’ historical scope and the boundary around unverified fixes alongside the company response.

items.title: OpenAI shares work on legacy programming languages
items.summary: OpenAI describes evaluations of building and migrating software in languages including COBOL and Fortran. These are company-reported results; preserving behavior in a real system still needs testing.

items.title: Chen welcomes Orchestra Bio
items.summary: Chen welcomed Orchestra Bio as OpenAI expands its life-sciences work. The announcement describes a business acquisition and research ambitions; it does not establish a clinical benefit.

items.title: Altman welcomes new interpretability work
items.summary: Altman welcomed Nick Cammarata’s work on understanding neural networks. The Goodfire essay presents a working hypothesis; this reaction is not independent validation or evidence that AI safety is solved.

items.title: Brockman introduces interactive answers in ChatGPT
items.summary: Brockman shared the Intelligent UI launch, describing interactive elements in ChatGPT responses. This is a company announcement; the interface is not independent evidence of answer accuracy.
